sentences.text: The reassembled holotype skeleton is currently displayed at the Museum am Löwentor in Stuttgart.
In May 1906, fossil trader Bernhard Hauff found a uniquely complete plesiosaur skeleton in discarded rocks near Holzmaden.
It took over nine months to remove 2.5 tonnes of chalkstone to expose and prepare the bones.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — was destroyed during a firestorm in Stuttgart on September 12, 1944.
Adam S. Smith and Peggy Vincent named the genus Meyerasaurus in 2010, establishing the valid species name Meyerasaurus victor.
The name honors German paleontologist Hermann von Meyer, who originally proposed the name Thaumatosaurus.
This animal belongs to the family Rhomaleosauridae.
Meyerasaurus lived in the early Toarcian stage of the Early Jurassic, approximately 183 to 180 million years ago.
Its habitat was the Posidonia Shale lagerstätte, a site famous for exceptional preservation.
In 2007, Adam Stuart Smith proposed creating a separate genus because he considered the original name Thaumatosaurus to be a nomen dubium.
